newsitem.title: UK: World Bank eyes mark zero-coupon bond - dealers.
newsitem.headline: World Bank eyes mark zero-coupon bond - dealers.

text.p: The World Bank may issue a zero-coupon bond for up to 2.0 billion marks, syndicate managers said on Thursday.
"A number of supranational borrowers are eyeing the sector, including the World Bank, and they may launch an issue next week," a syndicate official at a German bank said.
"For the World Bank an issue size of 1.5 to 2.0 billion marks would not be a problem," he said.
A Deutsche Bank unit launched a 1.0 billion mark 30-year zero-coupon bond on Tuesday at a 13.20 issue price. While the nominal value was high, only 130 million marks changed hands.
"The actual amount is quite small, but investors agree to tie up their money for a long time," said a Frankfurt-based new issues trader.

"Investors are keen on these deals because current low interest rates create appetite for anything with a bit of extra yield. Zero-coupon bonds have tax advantages, especially for borrowers like the World Bank," he said.

Although 30-year bonds have been the favoured maturity for zero-coupon deals, traders said the World Bank could launch a 20-year issue or otherwise choose a maturity to match a mark government benchmark such as the 2028 Bund.
